claims.text: The target material is an equiatomic or near-equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy with inherent compositional disorder.
The target CrMnFeCoNi alloy can be studied in an as-cast or as-sintered state.
A model combining ab initio defect perturbation theory, machine learning, and local-bonding descriptors will improve prediction of low phonon thermal conductivity in CrMnFeCoNi.
Machine-learning methods can link alloy-composition descriptors to target material properties.
Atomic-radius mismatch, elastic-modulus variation, and chemical disorder produce local lattice distortions.
Local bonding environments modulate the local lattice distortions in CrMnFeCoNi.
Chemical and structural disorder enhances phonon scattering and decreases phonon mean free path.
A decrease in phonon mean free path suppresses lattice thermal conductivity.
Adding local-bonding parameters will capture subtle structural features neglected by conventional models.
Adding local-bonding parameters will reduce thermal-conductivity prediction uncertainty.
The integrated model will predict lattice thermal conductivity to within ±10% of TDTR measurements.
The integrated model will provide more than a 25% improvement over current empirical or first-principles predictions.
Conventional empirical or standard first-principles models typically have uncertainties greater than ±10% for this problem.
Conventional models inadequately represent the complex disorder in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed model is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi between 300 and 600 K.
Lattice vibrations dominate thermal transport in CrMnFeCoNi over 300–600 K.
TDTR can provide experimental thermal-conductivity measurements for validating the model.
Deviation exceeding ±20% for a statistically significant set of samples will falsify the hypothesis.
Accurately representing compositional disorder, anharmonic effects, and bonding-descriptor selection is a major source of model uncertainty.
